chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “If it were proper for anyone to be stoned twice, the one who commits liwat would have been stoned.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.يُرْجَمَ: to be stoned as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What does a hadith from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام say about the punishment for liwat?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys the extreme severity of the legal punishment associated with liwat in Shia jurisprudential tradition. It is phrased as a forceful legal statement from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام emphasizing the gravity of the act.
